note: Offline snapshots, read by src/compliance/sanctions.ts. Each file is pinned by its SHA-256; a file that does not match is refused. Refreshing a snapshot is a reviewed commit (new file, new hash, new date), never an automatic download. Mainnet Bitcoin addresses only; the regtest demo never matches them unless a test list is added.

lists.title: OFAC SDN list: digital currency addresses, XBT (Bitcoin)
lists.authority: U.S. Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), Specially Designated Nationals list (sdn_advanced.xml)
lists.source: 0xB10C/ofac-sanctioned-digital-currency-addresses, branch lists, lists/sanctioned_addresses_XBT.txt (extracted nightly from OFAC's sdn_advanced.xml)
lists.licence: OFAC data: U.S. government work. Extraction tool: MIT (0xB10C). Names and programs are not in this file; look them up in the SDN list by address.
lists.caveat: A mirror of OFAC's list, not OFAC itself. Confirm against treasury.gov before relying on it in production.

lists.title: OpenSanctions il_mod_crypto (Israel NBCTF seized/sanctioned crypto wallets): Bitcoin-address wallets
lists.format: tsv: address, opensanctions entity id, holder name, currency, topics
lists.authority: Israel Ministry of Defense, National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing (NBCTF), as published by OpenSanctions
lists.source: OpenSanctions dataset il_mod_crypto version 20261017180205-ljh, entities.ftm.json (sha256 7d02319e383e69679bcf24d959d79f89eeed94a2bec1853fef63ccfd435beca4): every CryptoWallet whose currency is BTC or whose key is a Bitcoin address (some are Omni USDT on Bitcoin)
lists.licence: OpenSanctions data is CC BY-NC 4.0: free for non-commercial use (this hackathon demo); a commercial deployment needs an OpenSanctions data licence. To confirm with counsel.
lists.caveat: One OpenSanctions dataset, not the whole sanctions collection (307,454 entities, 77-460 MB exports), which a deployment would load from its own licensed copy.
